notes.title: Polysomnography Report
notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Polysomnography Report
Date: 09/26/2025
Patient: Sharan Wisozk, 86-year-old female

Diagnostic in-laboratory polysomnography performed 09/26/2025. The study assessed sleep patterns and breathing abnormalities throughout the night. Total apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) 40.2 events/hour. Central and mixed apneas comprised 18% of all events. Sleep architecture showed typical stage distribution with some fragmentation. The findings indicate severe sleep-disordered breathing with a significant proportion of central and mixed apneas. Clinical correlation and treatment planning are recommended based on these results.

Sleep Medicine Consultation Note
Date: 08/09/2026
Patient: Sharan Wisozk, 87-year-old female

Reason for Consultation:
Evaluation and management of sleep-related concerns.

History:
Ms. Wisozk presents for assessment of her sleep patterns and treatment adherence. She has been using CPAP therapy but reports difficulty tolerating the device.

Physical Examination:
BMI 25.9 kg/m2.

Assessment:
CPAP intolerance: download shows average use 1.9 hours per night on 33% of nights despite mask refitting; shared decision-making with the patient documented that CPAP is not tolerated.

Plan:
Discuss alternative treatment options and supportive measures to improve sleep quality. Continue monitoring and follow-up to reassess therapy effectiveness and patient comfort.

Summary:
Ms. Wisozk is an elderly female with documented CPAP intolerance despite efforts to optimize mask fit. Further management will focus on individualized approaches to address her sleep needs.
